official.description_text:
Postdoc in Computational Methods for Games and Multi-Agent Decision Making
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
Game theory is rapidly gaining traction in several engineering applications as the natural framework for multi-agent decision making. Yet, unlike optimization, game theory has no mature, general-purpose solvers. Computing an equilibrium of a multi-agent noncooperative game amounts to solving a large-scale generalized equation, and available solutions rely on restrictive assumptions, offer no control over which equilibrium is returned, and scale poorly with the size of the problem. This position addresses the computational side of this gap.
We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher with a solid background in one or more of the following areas: game theory, optimization algorithms, and numerical methods. The successful candidate will develop efficient algorithms and computational tools for equilibrium computation in multi-agent games. The work will focus on:
Scalable algorithms for various equilibrium problems in multi-agent games;
Open-source computational tools and benchmarks;
Application of game-theoretic solvers to multi-agent autonomous systems;
About WASP:
The position is affiliated with the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP), Sweden's largest individual research program ever. Read more
here.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
A strong foundation in mathematical tools relevant for the project.
A demonstrated record of research achievements and publications in high-impact venues in automatic control, optimization, or related fields.
Proficiency in scientific programming (e.g., Python, Julia, or C++) and experience implementing optimization algorithms.
Proven ability to work both independently and in interdisciplinary teams.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Expertise in operator theory, variational inequalities, or operator-splitting methods.
Contributions to optimization software.
Teaching abilities and experience mentoring master students.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge. (max 2 pages)
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Motivation letter (1 page max).
Research statement (1 pages max, excluding references).
Contact of two academic or professional references.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: A postdoctoral position at KTH focused on developing scalable algorithms and computational tools for equilibrium computation in multi-agent game theory, with applications to autonomous systems. The role emphasizes mathematical foundations, optimization algorithms, and scientific programming rather than human-centred research or immersive systems.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is centred on game-theoretic algorithms and multi-agent decision-making in autonomous systems. While the researcher has experience with multiplayer collaboration mechanics, the posting shows no engagement with human factors, learning outcomes, spatial cognition, or immersive interaction design. The thematic distance is substantial.

methodological_fit.rationale: The researcher has intermediate quantitative research and experimental design skills, but the position requires deep expertise in operator theory, variational inequalities, and operator-splitting methods—mathematical tools for algorithm development. The posting emphasizes 'mathematical tools', 'optimization algorithms', and 'numerical methods' as core requirements. The researcher's strength lies in user-centred empirical evaluation and XR application development, not computational mathematics or algorithm research.

growth_value.rationale: The position would develop scientific programming skills (Python, C++) and deepen quantitative/mathematical foundations, which could support future hybrid work. However, it offers negligible closure on the researcher's core capability gaps: advanced statistical modelling, eye-tracking and physiological sensing integration, or mixed-methods evaluation in immersive contexts. The domain (game-theoretic equilibrium computation) is orthogonal to spatial cognition and human-centred immersive research.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution with WASP funding backing (stable, prestigious program). Stockholm aligns with geographic preferences. However, the group's focus on computational methods and autonomous systems does not align with the researcher's target identity as a human-centred XR/HCI researcher. The postdoc would be a career detour away from the target trajectory toward doctoral or project positions in collaborative immersive systems and spatial learning.

eligibility_flags: Position requires a completed PhD; researcher currently holds MSc by Research (in progress). Eligibility requirement states degree must be held 'no later than the time the employment decision is made'—timing depends on MSc completion date and application/decision timeline.

Posting does not explicitly restrict non-EU citizens, but mentions potential security clearance under Swedish Protective Security Act (2018:585) if the role is classified as security-sensitive. Scope and impact of this requirement unclear from text.
risks: Substantial domain mismatch: game-theoretic algorithm development is fundamentally different from human-centred immersive research. Success would require developing expertise in advanced mathematics and optimization—areas not evidenced in the researcher's profile.

Career trajectory risk: accepting this postdoc would delay or redirect progress toward the target identity (human-centred XR/HCI researcher) and priority institutions (Aalto, TU Delft). Two years in computational game theory would not strengthen candidacy for immersive systems positions.
Qualification gap: the researcher has beginner-level statistics and no demonstrated experience with operator theory, variational inequalities, or numerical methods—all signalled as core to the role.
Postdoc timing: the researcher is still completing an MSc thesis. A postdoc is not aligned with stated target position types (doctoral researcher, PhD candidate, project researcher with PhD pathway).

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
